Article Title: Barefoot mom in sari runs 3km to win Rs 5k for kids' education
Article Text:
Ramabai ran 3km with the indomitable spirit of a mother competing for a cash prize

PUNE: Ramabai Ranvir had no idea what running a race meant. All she had heard was there was Rs 3,000 to be won if she finished first.So, the 47-year-old widow hopped onto the pickup with a group of police aspirants from the Beed academy where she worked, hoping to compete in what would be the first race of her life. It didn't bother her that she hadn't trained for the rigours of a long-distance run. It hardly mattered that she was the lone runner without shoes.In her sari, barefoot after her slippers gave up midway through the run, Ramabai ran 3km with the indomitable spirit of a mother competing for a cash prize that would ease her struggle to pay for her daughters' education."I ran like my life depended on it. I didn't know how much time I needed to cover the distance. I only sto-pped once I was past the finish line," she told TOI. "I am so happy they gave me Rs 5,000 instead of Rs 3,000. I bought notebooks and pens for my daughter Pooja. The remaining money is for Arti."Ramabai works in the kitchen at Dnyandeep Acad-emy, making over 200 chapatis a day for a monthly salary of Rs 9,000.The native of Potra, Hingoli, took the job to fund the education of her two daughters after her husband died in 2012.On Aug 28, her younger daughter Arti (20), a BSc computer science student who lives alone in Nanded, called asking for money for food and rent. Ramabai, who didn't have any cash to spare, had a sleepless night.At dawn, she heard the academy's trainers rounding up aspirants for a running competition nearby. She instantly decided to join in."There is no pain worse than that of not being able to take care of your children. The moment I came to know of the race, winning was the only thing on my mind."Datta Darade, who heads the academy, said Ramabai's determination moved him. The academy had enrolled her elder daughter Pooja (22) free of cost and given her employment and a room to stay in. "I was taking my students to the marathon. When Ramabai said she wanted to come along, I asked her, 'What will you do there?' She said, 'I will run.' I couldn't believe it when she won in the above-30 category."Pooja finished second in the 18-30 age group and won Rs 2,000. Arti said she was dumbstruck when her sister called to say their mother had won."Our mother studied till Class 7 and has worked all her life, not taking breaks even when she was unwell. She didn't hesitate to send me to Nanded for my studies. I am not surprised she decided to win a race for her family," she said.

Article Title: Alphonso Smith Jr. cause of death: How did the former Broncos cornerback die at 40?
Article Text:

Alphonso Smith Jr. cause of death : Reports say he died by suicide in Florida

Alphonso Smith Jr. made his name with Wake Forest before reaching the NFL

Former NFL cornerback Alphonso Smith Jr. died at 40 in Florida on Wednesday, September 2, 2026. News of his death came after the former Denver Broncos and Detroit Lions player shared a disturbing Facebook message about his personal struggles. His final words quickly drew attention as fans looked back at the career of a defensive back who once stood out at both Wake Forest and in the NFL.According to reports, Smith died by suicide in Florida. His final Facebook post added a painful layer to the news. He wrote about fighting personal demons, apologized to people he believed he had hurt and said he had needed help.According to various reports, Smith died by suicide at a housing community in Florida. The reports cited sources with direct knowledge of the situation. Smith was 40. His death came shortly after he posted a lengthy message on Facebook. The former cornerback opened up about serious personal struggles and described trying to fight what he called “demons.” He also spoke about painful experiences from his childhood and reflected on how those experiences had affected him.“Do not cry for me! I tried everything in my power to fight the demons behind the ones that someone put into ME!” Smith wrote in his final Facebook post.The message became even more concerning as Smith continued. He apologized to his children, family, friends and others he believed he had hurt. He also indicated that he had tried to get help.“I did not want to be that WAY! I know I have disappointed so many folks. This is a DEMON in me! But not only me! It’s EVERYONE! I have HURT so many! I needed help & did not get it,” Smith wrote on Facebook.He ended the post with another apology and the words, “I am SORRY! THIS IS IT!”The message has since become a major part of the coverage surrounding his death. Still, the circumstances of his final moments remain private, and reports have offered only limited details about what happened in Florida.Smith’s football story started at Wake Forest, where he developed into one of the ACC’s top defensive backs. He finished his college career with 21 interceptions, a Wake Forest record and an ACC mark at the time.The Denver Broncos selected Smith No. 37 overall in the second round of the 2009 NFL Draft. He played 15 games during his rookie season before Denver traded him to the Detroit Lions in September 2010.The move gave Smith his best NFL opportunity. In 2010, he started 10 games for Detroit and recorded a team-high five interceptions. He also returned one interception for a touchdown and finished the season with 39 tackles.Smith remained with the Lions through the 2012 season. Across four NFL seasons from 2009 through 2012, he played 42 games and finished with 88 tackles and eight interceptions.His NFL career ended in 2012, but his accomplishments at Wake Forest and his time with Denver and Detroit remain part of his football legacy. Now, following his death on September 2, 2026, Smith is being remembered for far more than his years on the field.

News of his death came after the former denver broncos and detroit lions player shared a disturbing facebook message about his personal struggles.

Article Title: Argentina can't retire Messi's legendary No.10 because of the same FIFA rule that stopped them honouring Maradona in 2002
Article Text:
Argentina cannot retire Messi’s iconic No.10 because FIFA requires every World Cup squad number from 1 to 26 to be assigned/ Image: file

Argentina wanted to retire Maradona’s No.10 too

A pedestrian carries a bucket past graffiti depicting late soccer legend Diego Maradona in Buenos Aires, Argentina, Monday, April 13, 2026. (AP Photo/Rodrigo Abd)

Why FIFA will not let Argentina retire the shirt

Argentinian super fan Miloslav Urbanec shows his statue of Diego Maradona on a day of the World Cup semifinal match between Argentina and England, in the village of Bukovka, Czech Republic, Wednesday, July 15, 2026. (AP Photo/Petr David Josek)

Must read:

Messi’s No.10 has become impossible to separate from his legacy

Sport

Must read:

The next No.10 will inherit a shirt unlike any other

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Lionel Messi’s retirement from international football has left Argentina with a question that feels almost impossible to answer: what happens to the No.10 shirt now? For many supporters, the obvious answer is to retire it forever. Messi wore it for two decades, became Argentina’s most-capped player and all-time leading scorer, and turned the shirt into one of the most recognisable symbols in world football. But Argentina has tried to do this before, when Diego Maradona was the player being honoured, and FIFA stopped it. More than two decades later, the same regulation stands in the way of giving Messi the ultimate tribute.The idea of retiring Argentina’s No.10 is not new, and its strongest precedent comes from the country’s other footballing icon.On 25 September 2001, the Argentine Football Association voted unanimously, on the initiative of then-president Julio Grondona, to retire the No.10 shirt in honour of Maradona.The plan was to put the decision into effect before the 2002 World Cup, and at the time it appeared to be settled. Argentine newspaper Olé even ran a front-page headline declaring: "It is God's will."There was, however, one problem: FIFA had its own rules governing squad numbers at its tournaments.FIFA rejected Argentina’s request, meaning the No.10 could not simply disappear from the World Cup squad. Ariel "El Burrito" Ortega ultimately wore the shirt for Argentina at the 2002 tournament, becoming the player who wore the famous number most prominently between the Maradona and Messi eras.The significance of that episode has returned now that Messi has stepped away from the national team.This time, it is not Maradona’s name attached to the request. It is Messi’s.The obstacle is not a lack of willingness from Argentina. It is the numbering system FIFA applies to its official tournaments.According to Marca, FIFA regulations require tournament squad lists for competitions such as the World Cup and Copa America to use consecutive numbers from 1 to 26. Every player selected for the 26-man squad must therefore have a number, with none omitted.That makes retiring the No.10 impossible in an official tournament.Argentina could want to leave the number untouched, supporters could overwhelmingly back the idea and the Argentine Football Association could decide that nobody should wear it again, but the regulations would still require the No.10 to be assigned to somebody when the team enters a tournament governed by FIFA's squad-number rules.In other words, Argentina cannot simply submit a 26-man squad numbered 1 through 9 and 11 through 27, or leave the No.10 blank as a permanent tribute to Messi. The numbering requirement creates a direct conflict with the idea of permanently retiring the shirt.That is exactly what happened with Maradona.The regulation therefore means Messi's No.10 can be treated differently in friendly matches, where Argentina could choose not to use the number, but the situation changes as soon as the national team enters an official tournament.The desire to retire the shirt is understandable because Messi did far more than simply inherit Maradona's number.He wore No.10 for Argentina for roughly two decades and leaves the national team as its all-time leading scorer and most-capped player. His international career also transformed the meaning of the shirt for another generation of Argentine supporters, just as Maradona had done before him.That is why the debate is not really about who deserves to wear the number next. It is about whether anybody should wear it at all.The Argentine Football Association has previously expressed a clear desire to retire the shirt once Messi ended his international career.In 2024, AFA president Claudio Tapia told: "The national team's number 10 shirt will be retired when Messi ends his international career."Tapia's comments made the association's intention clear, but the practical problem was always going to be FIFA's tournament regulations.The situation leaves Argentina with an unusual compromise. The No.10 could effectively be reserved as Messi's number whenever the team plays certain friendlies, allowing the association and supporters to honour him without giving the shirt to another player.But when the next World Cup or Copa America arrives, the number cannot simply be erased from Argentina's squad list.Someone will have to wear it.That leaves Argentina facing another difficult question: if the No.10 cannot be retired, who takes it?Messi's successor will inevitably inherit a shirt carrying the weight of both him and Maradona. It is one thing to wear the No.10 for Argentina; it is another to wear the number that has belonged to two of the country's greatest footballers.Several names could enter the conversation, including Alexis Mac Allister, Enzo Fernández, Thiago Almada and Nico Paz.According to ESPN Argentina insider Federico Bueno, Argentina have an internal plan for Paz to take the No.10 if Lionel Scaloni renews his contract as head coach, with negotiations expected to take place in the coming months.For now, though, the immediate reality is simpler: Messi's No.10 cannot be permanently removed from Argentina's official tournament squad.Maradona's Argentina tried it in 2001 and FIFA said no. More than 20 years later, the same rule means Messi's shirt faces the same fate.
Article Summary: Lionel messi’s retirement from international football has left argentina with a question that feels almost impossible to answer: what happens to the no.10 shirt now? For many supporters, the obvious answer is to retire it forever. Argentina has tried to do this before, when diego maradona was the player being honoured, and fifa stopped it.

Article Title: Naomi Osaka reveals “long bouts of depression” as tennis superstar makes powerful stand for her wellbeing
Article Text:
Naomi Osaka (Getty Images)

Naomi Osaka and the French Open controversy

Naomi Osaka’s mental health message drew support

In May 2021, Naomi Osaka made a decision that shook the tennis world. The four-time Grand Slam champion withdrew from the French Open after refusing post-match media conferences, saying she was protecting her mental health. What followed was a wider debate about athletes, media duties and the pressure that comes with competing under a global spotlight.The controversy began before Osaka even played her opening match at Roland Garros. The Japanese star announced that she would not attend news conferences during the tournament because of the anxiety she experienced around speaking to the media.After beating Romania’s Patricia Maria Tig in straight sets, Osaka was fined $15,000 for skipping her post-match media duties. The situation escalated when the four Grand Slam organisers warned that continued refusal could result in heavier fines and possible suspension.Osaka then chose to leave the tournament.Her decision was not simply about avoiding questions after matches. In her statement, she explained the personal struggle behind it."The truth is I have suffered long bouts of depression since the US Open in 2018 and I have had a really hard time coping with that."She also described how social anxiety affected her around tournaments."Anyone that knows me knows I am introverted and anyone that has seen me at tournaments will notice that I'm often wearing headphones as that helps dull my social anxiety."Those words changed the tone of the conversation. What had initially looked like a dispute over media obligations became a much larger discussion about the emotional demands placed on elite athletes.Osaka acknowledged that her timing could have been better, but she stood by her decision to put her wellbeing first.I never wanted to be a distraction and I accept my timing was not ideal and my message could have been clearer. More importantly, I would never trivialise mental health or use the term lightly."The truth is I have suffered long bouts of depression since the US Open in 2018 and I have had a really hard time coping with that."Anyone that knows me knows I am introverted and anyone that has seen me at tournaments will notice that I'm often wearing headphones as that helps dull my social anxiety."Though the tennis press has always been kind to me (and I want to apologise to all the cool journalists who I may have hurt), I am not a natural public speaker and get huge waves of anxiety before I speak to the world's media."I get really nervous and find it stressful to always try to engage and give you the best answers I can."So here in Paris I was already feeling vulnerable and anxious, so I thought it was better to exercise self-care and skip the press conferences. I announced it preemptively because I do feel like the rules are quite outdated in parts and I wanted to highlight that."I wrote privately to the tournament apologising and saying that I would be more than happy to speak with them after the tournament as the Slams are intense."I'm going to take some time away from the court now, but when the time is right I really want to work with the Tour to discuss ways we can make things better for the players, press and fans."
Article Summary: Naomi osaka withdrew from the french open after refusing post-match media conferences. The four-time grand slam champion said she was protecting her mental health. Her decision sparked a wider debate about athletes, media duties and the pressure that comes with competing under a global spotlight.

Article Title: Travis Kelce health scare sparks Chiefs concern days before 2026 season opener

Travis Kelce’s latest absence has put Kansas City Chiefs fans on alert just days before the team opens its 2026 campaign. The veteran tight end missed Kansas City’s annual kickoff luncheon on September 1 after reportedly feeling “under the weather. ” While there is no indication of a serious health issue, the timing has naturally drawn attention as Kelce prepares for another demanding NFL season.The update came through Kansas City Star reporter Pete Sweeney, who cited longtime Chiefs radio voice Mitch Holthus when reporting Kelce’s absence.“Travis Kelce is not at the Chiefs' annual kickoff luncheon. Under the weather, per Mitch Holthus,” Sweeney reported.That remains the clearest information available about Kelce’s condition. Neither the Chiefs nor the player has indicated that the illness is serious, and there has been no confirmation that it will prevent him from taking the field when Kansas City begins its season.Still, missing a major team event so close to opening day was enough to raise eyebrows.Kelce has plenty of motivation entering his 14th NFL season. The 36-year-old tight end chose to continue his career after considering retirement, and his comments during the offseason suggested that he still believes he has more to accomplish.“I've had a lot of success in the NFL, but I'm still reaching for that perfection,” Kelce told Vogue. “I still haven't played the perfect game.”His ambition has not faded with age. If anything, Kelce appears determined to make another serious run at success alongside quarterback Patrick Mahomes “Year 14, baby, I'm fired up. Every year there's a chance to do something special, but especially coming into this year, getting Pat [Mahomes] back and wiping the slate clean.”Kelce’s health update is particularly significant because he remains an important part of Kansas City’s offensive plans. Last season, he finished with 76 receptions for 851 yards. That followed a career-low 823 receiving yards in 2024, leading to questions about how much longer he can maintain his elite production.Chiefs coach Andy Reid, however, has continued to praise Kelce’s work ethic and conditioning.“You have examples like Kelce - he's the oldest guy on the team and came out every day and worked to where you had to yank him out of there to give him a breather,” Reid said.There is also history within reach.Kelce currently has 13,002 career receiving yards. He needs 45 more to move past Jason Witten and claim second place among tight ends on the NFL’s all-time receiving yardage list.For now, Kansas City has little reason to panic. Kelce was simply reported to be under the weather, with no further details released. The next few days should provide a clearer picture of whether the brief absence is nothing more than a minor setback or something the Chiefs need to monitor before kickoff.
Article Summary: Travis kelce missed kansas city's annual kickoff luncheon on september 1. The 36-year-old tight end was reportedly feeling “under the weather. ” there is no indication of a serious health issue, but the timing has naturally drawn attention.

Article Title: "She’s the breadwinner and doesn’t want money arguments": Lewis Hamilton and Kim Kardashian spark fresh buzz over viral claim about their relationship and finances
Article Text:
Kim Kardashian and Lewis Hamilton.(Image via Getty Images)

Lewis Hamilton did not reportedly make the viral money confession

Viral Lewis Hamilton and Kim Kardashian claim lacks credible evidence

false or unverified

A viral social media post is making a striking claim about Lewis Hamilton and Kim Kardashian, but the quote attached to it does not appear to be genuine. The post alleges that Hamilton said Kardashian pays for everything in their relationship and would continue doing so if they married. There is no credible interview or verified statement supporting those words, making the screenshot a classic example of how celebrity misinformation can spread quickly online.The post circulating online attributes a lengthy statement to Hamilton:“Since we started moving together, Kim hasn’t allowed me to pay for anything. Even though I make enough money from Formula 1, she prefers it this way. She’s the breadwinner and doesn’t want money arguments to ever come between us. She’s even comfortable keeping things this way if we eventually get married.”The wording may look convincing at first glance, but the post provides no interview, publication, video or original statement to establish where Hamilton supposedly said it.That is an important detail. A quote involving two of the world's most recognizable celebrities can travel widely within hours, especially when it touches on money, romance and marriage.But the number of views or reposts does not make a claim authentic.Current reporting does confirm that Hamilton and Kardashian have been romantically linked in 2026. Their relationship became increasingly public during the year, with reports documenting appearances together and Kardashian making the relationship public on social media.That real relationship, however, does not validate every quote attached to their names.The biggest warning sign is the absence of a traceable source for Hamilton's alleged confession. The screenshot comes from a social media account rather than a recognised interview or direct post from Hamilton.That distinction matters because fabricated celebrity quotes often borrow real relationships and add dramatic personal details. The result can look like news while offering no reliable evidence.There is also no reason to treat the supposed marriage comment as established fact. While recent entertainment reports have described Hamilton and Kardashian's relationship as serious and have discussed long-term possibilities, those reports are separate from the viral money claim.In fact, the pair's relationship itself only became public during 2026 after months of speculation. Kardashian and Hamilton have since appeared together at events and shared glimpses of their time together, giving fans genuine material to discuss.The viral quote is therefore best treated as, not as a genuine Lewis Hamilton revelation.For readers, the lesson is simple: when a celebrity quote makes an unusually dramatic claim about money, marriage or private life, check for the original interview before accepting a screenshot as fact. In this case, the relationship is real, but the alleged Hamilton confession is not supported by credible evidence.
Article Summary: Viral lewis hamilton and kim kardashian claim lacks credible evidence. The post alleges that hamilton said kardashian pays for everything in their relationship and would continue doing so if they married. There is no credible interview or verified statement supporting those words, making the screenshot a classic example of how celebrity misinformation can spread quickly online.

Article Title: Philadelphia 76ers legend reacts to heartfelt Naomi Osaka tribute as US Open outfit proved to be love letter to the NBA icon
Article Text:
Naomi Osaka. Image via: Robert Prange/ Getty Images

Naomi Osaka's US Open outfit pays tribute to Allen Iverson

Allen Iverson reacts to Naomi Osaka's tribute

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Osaka's run of statement outfits continues this season

Naomi Osaka opened her US Open campaign with an outfit built entirely around one man, and it is Allen Iverson. The four-time Grand Slam champion walked onto Arthur Ashe Stadium wearing his signature headband and arm sleeve, tucked under a gray hooded robe covered in newspaper clippings from her own career, paired with a wide, floor-length skirt.She won the match in straight sets, but the outfit had people talking before a ball was even struck. By Monday night, Iverson had noticed too, and he had something to say about it.Naomi Osaka beat unseeded Russian Anastasia Zakharova 7-6, 7-6 in her opening match, but the real story arrived before the first serve. Her robe, worn as she entered Ashe, was stitched with burnout newspaper clippings tracing her own career, a nod to Iverson's habit of turning up in whatever he wanted rather than what the league expected. She kept it simple when asked why. "It's my tribute to Iverson. I really like him a lot," she said afterward.The look was part of a broader Nike push linking tennis to basketball at this year's tournament. Aryna Sabalenka wore a mesh jersey in an orange shade tied to the Knicks for her own first-round win earlier that day.Osaka had already signaled where her loyalty sat days before, wearing a shirt printed with an old SLAM magazine cover of Iverson and calling him someone who reshaped how NBA players dress, on and off the court.Osaka admitted she had never actually met Iverson, only that she hoped he would see the outfit. And he did. The Hall of Famer posted his reaction on Instagram within hours: "Wow, what a honor!! BIG FAN can't wait to meet you."Designers Téla D'Amore and Ev Bravado, who built the piece, said Osaka and stylist Law Roach sent them two reference photos of Iverson in his headband, then gave them roughly 30 hours to construct the rest around that image.The result carried Iverson's off-court signature almost exactly: the sweats, the sleeve, the headband worn low.This is far from Osaka's first fashion statement of the year. At the Australian Open, she arrived under a wide-brimmed veil and parasol in a jellyfish-inspired look. At the French Open, she unveiled a black corset made from her own old Nike gear before switching into a gold dress she compared to the Eiffel Tower at night. At Wimbledon, she worked within the tournament's all-white rule to build a kimono-inspired outfit honoring Japanese design traditions.Osaka finished Monday's win with 11 aces against three double faults, despite 30 unforced errors along the way. She now moves on to face Kateřina Siniaková in the second round on Wednesday.
Article Summary: Naomi osaka wore allen iverson's signature headband and arm sleeve to the us open. The four-time grand slam champion beat anastasia zakharova in straight sets. The outfit was part of a broader nike push linking tennis to basketball at the tournament.

The Rams eventually won Super Bowl LVI in 2022, doing it inside their own stadium.But the Rams were only one piece of the puzzle.Through Kroenke Sports & Entertainment, his portfolio also includes theandin the Premier League. And now the Angels are joining the group.Kroenke's major-league portfolio now stretches across six major sports leagues once the Angels transaction is completed:The Angels will be Kroenke's first MLB franchise.The six-league description refers to the six major competitions represented by those teams. His sports holdings also include the, meaning his wider professional-sports portfolio reaches beyond those six leagues.There is also an unusual ownership structure surrounding some of the teams. Because of NFL ownership rules, Kroenke transferred his ownership interests in the Nuggets and Avalanche to his wife, Ann Walton Kroenke, in 2015, although they remain part of the broader Kroenke Sports & Entertainment empire.The eye-catching part of Kroenke's portfolio isn't simply its size.It is the number of championships his teams have collected.The Rams won the Super Bowl in 2022.The Colorado Avalanche won the Stanley Cup in 2022.The Denver Nuggets captured their first NBA championship in 2023.And Arsenal added another major success to Kroenke's collection in 2026, winning the Premier League. ESPN noted that four of Kroenke's teams had won championships in their respective sports within the previous five years.That gives Kroenke something very few owners can claim: a sports portfolio that has produced championship success across multiple major leagues and two continents.

Article Title: Inspiring story on parenthood: “I gave up my childhood to be able to have my children’s childhood” – What Andre Agassi and wife Steffi Graf’s parenting journey teaches about raising a family
Article Text:
Inspiring story on parenthood: “I gave up my childhood to be able to have my children’s childhood” – What Andre Agassi and wife Steffi Graf’s parenting journey teaches about raising a family

What did Andre Agassi mean when he said, “I gave up my childhood to be able to have my children’s childhood”?

How did becoming a father change Agassi’s view of his own childhood?

How did Steffi Graf fit into Agassi’s approach to raising their children?

What does Agassi’s quote tell us about his idea of parenthood?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Andre Agassi’s words, “I gave up my childhood to be able to have my children’s childhood,” offer a deeply personal look at how becoming a parent changed the tennis legend’s view of his own life. Agassi grew up in a world where tennis was not simply a sport but a major part of his everyday life, with intense training and expectations starting at a very young age. Years later, after becoming one of tennis’ biggest stars, he and his wife, fellow tennis legend Steffi Graf, built a family life around their two children, Jaden and Jaz. For Agassi, watching his children grow gave him the chance to experience some of the simple moments of childhood that he felt he had missed himself.The quote is closely connected to Agassi’s own experience growing up. He started playing tennis as a young child and was pushed toward the sport by his father, Mike Agassi. His father had a clear dream for him: he wanted his son to become one of the best tennis players in the world.That dream eventually came true.Agassi went on to become world No. 1 and won eight Grand Slam singles titles during his career. But reaching that level meant spending much of his childhood training, competing and preparing for professional tennis.For a young child, that kind of life can leave little room for ordinary experiences. Instead of having complete freedom to decide how he wanted to spend his time, Agassi’s days were largely connected to tennis.That is where his famous quote becomes especially powerful.When he says he “gave up” his childhood, he is looking back at the years he spent becoming a professional athlete. But he is also talking about what those sacrifices eventually allowed him to do.His success gave him the freedom to step away from tennis and spend more time with his family. It allowed him to be present as his children grew up.In other words, Agassi may have missed parts of his own childhood, but later he had the opportunity to sit beside his children and watch them experience theirs. For him, that became a kind of second chance.Fatherhood gave Andre Agassi a different way of looking at his past. When he watched Jaden and Jaz grow up, he could see the small moments of childhood from a parent’s point of view.He could watch them discover what they liked, make their own choices and develop personalities separate from their famous parents.Those moments were very different from the childhood Agassi had experienced.His early years were strongly connected to the tennis court. His father believed that constant practice and discipline were necessary if Andre Agassi was going to become a champion. That approach helped produce an incredible tennis career, but it also meant that Agassi’s childhood was far from ordinary.As a father, he wanted something different for his children.Instead of seeing childhood as preparation for a future career, Agassi wanted Jaden and Jaz to enjoy the years they were living through.That is one of the most important ideas behind his quote. He was not simply saying that he wanted to give his children more material things or better opportunities. He wanted to give them time.Time to grow.Time to explore.Time to make mistakes.Time to decide what they wanted for themselves.This became especially important because Agassi knew from personal experience how powerful parental expectations can be. He had spent years trying to become the player his father wanted him to be. As a parent, he had the chance to make sure his own children did not feel that same pressure.Steffi Graf’s role in the family’s story is important because she understood Agassi’s world better than almost anyone. Like her husband, Graf was introduced to tennis at a very young age and went on to become one of the greatest players in the history of the sport.Steffi Graf won 22 Grand Slam singles titles and spent years at the top of women’s tennis before retiring in 1999. Agassi and Graf later married and raised their two children, Jaden and Jaz.Together, they had something unusual in common: both parents knew exactly what it took to become a tennis champion, but they also knew the pressure that came with that journey.That understanding appears to have influenced the way they raised their children.Despite having two parents who were global tennis stars, Jaden and Jaz were not simply expected to follow the same path.Jaden developed a passion for baseball rather than choosing tennis as his main sport. Jaz has also been able to follow her own interests. Andre Agassi and Graf have supported their children without making their parents’ careers the center of their lives.That is particularly meaningful when viewed alongside Agassi’s quote.The couple had already achieved what many athletes spend their entire lives chasing. They did not need their children to continue that legacy for them.Instead, they could give their children something that both parents understood the value of: choice.Agassi has also spoken warmly about Graf and the role she plays in his life. Their shared experience in professional sports gave them an understanding of the demands and sacrifices that come with elite competition.For their family, giving their children the freedom to choose their own paths became more important than creating another generation of tennis champions.At its heart, Agassi’s quote is about turning his own difficult experiences into something positive for his children.He cannot go back and change the childhood he had. He cannot erase the years of training, pressure and expectations that came with becoming a tennis player.But he can choose what kind of childhood his own children experience.That is what makes the quote about much more than tennis.Many parents work hard because they want their children to have opportunities they did not have themselves. Agassi’s story takes that idea one step further. His goal was not simply to provide his children with a comfortable life. He wanted to be present for the experiences that make childhood special.His words also show that parenthood can change the way people understand their own past.The same childhood that once felt difficult to Agassi became part of what helped him understand his children better. His experiences taught him what pressure can feel like, which may have made him more aware of the importance of giving his own children freedom.And Steffi Graf was there beside him, bringing her own experience as a former champion and a parent.Together, Agassi and Graf chose not to make their children’s lives about living up to their parents’ names. They allowed Jaden and Jaz to build identities of their own.That may be the most powerful part of Agassi’s words.He spent his childhood becoming a tennis champion. But when he became a father, he did not want his children to spend their childhood becoming something for him.He wanted to watch them simply be children.So, when Agassi says, “I gave up my childhood to be able to have my children’s childhood,” he is not only talking about sacrifice. He is talking about perspective, presence and love.He gave years of his life to tennis. Those years helped him become a champion and eventually gave him the freedom to step back and focus on his family.For Agassi, one of the greatest rewards was not another trophy or achievement. It was being able to watch his children grow up on their own terms, with Graf by his side.That is what makes his quote so relatable. Parenthood does not allow us to rewrite our own childhoods, but it can give us the chance to create a different childhood for the next generation.
Article Summary: Tennis legend andre agassi said he gave up his childhood to have his children's childhood. The quote is closely connected to agassi's own experience growing up. Agassi grew up in a world where tennis was not simply a sport but a major part of his everyday life. Andre agassi and steffi graf have two children, jaden and jaz.

Article Title: “Three-against-one situation”: El Rubius opens up on being “targeted” in MrBeast’s viral $1M challenge

El Rubius reflects on a tough and “unfair” exit

Some viewers believe intense competitions like this naturally lead to uneven situations. Others feel Rubius may have had a point about being singled out. Either way, his words have added a human layer to a challenge that many only saw as entertainment.Speaking through an Instagram Story, Rubius did not hide his frustration, but he also made sure to thank his supporters. He said, "Guys, I just got knocked out of the game. It was a bit of an unfair elimination, but hey, at least I managed to walk away with $50,000 for you all, which I’ve already distributed. It went to the mods, the subs, and the non-subs alike."He further added, "I’m happy, of course, though admittedly, it was incredibly tough.I wasn't really a fan of the challenge itself, either. Sorry, I’m being a bit toxic right now, but let's just hope the MrBeast team doesn't see this! Guys, thank you all so much. Article Title: Mike Tyson started keeping pigeons as a bullied Brooklyn boy, finding love and comfort in them; decades later, he still has hundreds of birds across the US
Article Text:
Mike Tyson's connection with pigeons began in Brooklyn

One pigeon became connected to his first fight

Pigeons remained with him as boxing took over

Tyson treated pigeon racing almost like another form of competition

His collection has been much larger than a normal backyard flock

Tyson still has hundreds of pigeons decades later

From Brooklyn rooftops to birds across America

Long before Mike Tyson became one of boxing's most feared heavyweight champions, pigeons were a source of love and comfort for him. Tyson has recalled being bullied as a child growing up in Brooklyn and finding refuge in the pigeons he kept, saying that spending time with them helped take his mind off the world around him and the people who picked on him. The birds became so important that Tyson later described pigeons as the first loving relationship he ever had. They were also unexpectedly connected to the beginning of his fighting life. Tyson has said that when a neighbourhood bully killed one of his pigeons in front of him, he fought back, marking what he has described as his first fight. More than five decades later, his fascination with the birds remains strong. In March 2025, Tyson said he owned hundreds of pigeons, perhaps as many as 1,000, across the US.Tyson's relationship with pigeons goes back to his childhood in Brooklyn, where he became involved with the birds long before he entered boxing. His affection for them developed at a time when he was dealing with difficulties at home and being bullied by other children. In a 2011 New Yorker account, Tyson explained that spending time with pigeons helped take his mind away from the world he was living in and the people who bullied him.The birds gave him something to care for and a space where he could escape from the pressures around him. Tyson has also recalled that he was around 11 when pigeons became closely connected with his life and eventual involvement in fighting.Tyson's attachment to pigeons was unusually deep for a childhood hobby. He has described them as his first loving relationship, a phrase that captures how emotionally important the birds became to him. His interest was not simply about owning animals. He spent time caring for them, watching them fly and becoming familiar with the different types of pigeons and their behaviour. The rooftop pigeon coops of Brooklyn became a place where he could spend time away from the difficulties of his childhood. The New Yorker reported Tyson explaining that the birds helped him take his mind off the world around him, particularly the people who bullied him.Perhaps the most remarkable part of Tyson's pigeon story is the connection he has drawn between the birds and his development as a fighter. According to accounts of Tyson's childhood, a neighbourhood bully took one of his pigeons, killed it and threw the bird at Tyson. Tyson reacted by punching the boy. CBS reported in 2011 that Tyson's first punch came after a neighbourhood bully killed one of his beloved pigeons. Tyson has repeatedly told versions of this story and has connected the incident with the beginning of his fighting instinct. It should be treated as Tyson's own account of an important moment in his life, rather than as proof that the incident alone caused his boxing career.As Tyson's life changed and he rose through the boxing world, his relationship with pigeons did not disappear. He continued keeping birds even after becoming heavyweight champion and one of the most recognisable athletes in the world. The New Yorker reported in 2011 that Tyson had raised pigeons before he began boxing, while earlier reporting documented his continued involvement with pigeon keeping in adulthood. The contrast was striking. Outside the ring Tyson became known for extraordinary power and aggression, yet around his pigeons he displayed a markedly gentler side. One account described him gently kissing a pigeon on the beak before releasing it, highlighting how different his relationship with the birds could look from his public image as a fighter.Tyson eventually took his lifelong interest further by becoming involved in competitive homing-pigeon racing. In 2011, Animal Planet's six-part series Taking on Tyson followed the former heavyweight champion as he attempted to build a team and compete in the sport. CBS reported that Tyson was a longtime pigeon fancier but a novice at racing, with experienced racers helping him learn the competitive side of the hobby. Homing-pigeon racing involves releasing birds away from their home lofts and timing how quickly they return. The races can progress from relatively short distances to hundreds of miles.The competitive element appealed to Tyson because it gave him another form of challenge after years in boxing. His involvement was not limited to watching birds fly. He learned about breeding, training and preparing pigeons for races and worked with experienced people in the sport. The 2011 series showed Tyson moving into a world that was unfamiliar to him despite his lifelong experience with pigeons. His passion also attracted controversy. Animal rights organisation PETA criticised his involvement in pigeon racing, arguing that racing could expose birds to injuries, exhaustion and other risks. Tyson's supporters and people involved in the sport, meanwhile, presented it as an established competitive tradition centred on the birds' homing ability.Tyson's pigeon collection has varied considerably in size over the years, and figures reported at different times should not be treated as a single permanent total. In 2011, The New Yorker reported that Tyson had around 3,000 birds, while other contemporary accounts also put his collection in the thousands. At other points, reports focused on much smaller numbers kept at particular homes. These differences are important because Tyson has maintained birds in different locations and because the size of a racing or breeding collection can change over time. What is clear is that his involvement has extended far beyond keeping a handful of pet pigeons.The most useful current figure comes directly from Tyson himself. In a March 2025 interview with PEOPLE, the then-58-year-old Tyson said he owned hundreds of pigeons, adding that the total could be “maybe a thousand”. He said the birds were spread across California, New Jersey, Florida and Las Vegas. This is the strongest basis for saying that Tyson still keeps hundreds of pigeons across the US. Because the figure is Tyson's own estimate rather than an independently verified count, it is more accurate to report it as hundreds, possibly around 1,000, rather than stating that he definitely owns exactly 1,000 birds.Tyson's latest comments make clear that pigeons are not simply a nostalgic reminder of his childhood. He told PEOPLE that he has been involved with pigeons for longer than he has done anything else, including boxing. He also said that pigeons had both got him into trouble and got him out of trouble and described them as something that had been part of his entire life. His remark that boxing is over but pigeons are still here neatly captures the unusual longevity of the relationship. The heavyweight championship years came and went, but the birds remained a constant presence.The geography of Tyson's pigeon keeping has changed dramatically since his childhood. What began with birds around Brooklyn's rooftops eventually became a passion involving lofts and birds in different parts of the country. His 2025 account places pigeons in California, New Jersey, Florida and Las Vegas, showing that the hobby has followed him through several stages of his adult life. Yet the basic attraction appears unchanged. Tyson still photographs and makes videos with his birds and has even included them in promotional material. For someone whose public identity was built around violence and competition, his decades-long devotion to pigeons offers a very different picture of the man away from the boxing ring.
Article Summary: Mike tyson's relationship with pigeons goes back to his childhood in brooklyn. He became involved with the birds long before he entered boxing. His affection for them developed at a time when he was dealing with difficulties at home and being bullied by other children.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Meryl Streep: “The formula of happiness and success is just,…” - a powerful reflection on authenticity
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Meryl Streep (Photo - @merylstreep)

Quote of the day by Meryl Streep

“The formula of happiness and success is just, being actually yourself, in the most vivid possible way you can.”

Where this line actually comes from

What the quote genuinely means

Why this idea still genuinely matters today

The idea is genuinely about self-knowledge as much as confidence

The same achievement can genuinely mean very different things

Real authenticity genuinely comes with difficult choices attached

Comparison can genuinely blur individual identity

Other memorable quotes by Meryl Streep

“The great gift of human beings is that we have the power of empathy.”

“You can't get spoiled if you do your own ironing.”

“I want to feel my life while I'm in it.”

“Acting is not about being someone different. It's finding the similarity in what is apparently different, then finding myself in there.”

How to apply this quote in daily life

Why these words still inspire millions

Some of the most memorable advice about success is powerful because it makes a complicated idea sound surprisingly simple. Meryl Streep ’s widely shared observation is a good example. “The formula of happiness and success is just, being actually yourself, in the most vivid possible way you can.” On the surface, it sounds like familiar advice about being yourself. The deeper message is about resisting the pressure to build a life around somebody else’s expectations or definition of success. Streep’s words connect happiness and achievement to the same thing: understanding who you are and having the confidence to live accordingly.The quote has circulated for years with Streep’s name attached to it and appears in several established collections of her sayings, including a Times of India compilation. However, an easily accessible primary interview or transcript establishing exactly when she first said it is difficult to locate, making it safer to describe the line as widely attributed to Meryl Streep. The thought itself fits closely with other remarks she has made about identity and acting, including her observation that acting involves finding something of herself within someone who initially appears different.The quote is built around the difference between living as yourself and living according to a version of yourself designed for other people. “Being actually yourself” means recognising your own values, interests and ambitions instead of automatically accepting whatever society considers impressive. The phrase “in the most vivid possible way” takes that idea further by suggesting that authenticity should become visible in the way a person works, creates, communicates and makes decisions. It is not simply about knowing who you are, but allowing that identity to shape the life you build.The observation feels particularly relevant in an age of constant comparison. Social media places other people’s careers, relationships, appearances and achievements in front of us throughout the day, often without showing the uncertainty or failure behind them. Comparison can motivate people, but problems begin when inspiration turns into imitation and somebody else’s life starts looking like a blueprint. Streep’s words remind us that another person’s success can show what is possible without deciding what our own success should look like.“Be yourself” sounds like advice about confidence, but it also requires knowing what genuinely matters to you. That means distinguishing between ambitions you truly want and those pursued mainly because they impress other people. Being authentic does not mean refusing to change; it means growing because experience has changed you, not because you are constantly trying to meet somebody else’s expectations.An achievement is not automatically fulfilling simply because other people recognise it as success. A promotion may be exactly what one person wants while leaving another stuck in work they no longer enjoy. Money, status and recognition can create opportunity, but they cannot determine whether a particular life feels meaningful. Streep’s point is that external success matters most when it still feels like your own.Being yourself is not always comfortable. It may mean choosing a career others question, admitting that an old ambition no longer suits you or accepting that not everybody will approve of your choices. Authenticity therefore does not guarantee praise or certainty, but Streep’s words suggest that happiness built entirely around other people’s approval is even more fragile.The more closely people measure themselves against others, the easier it becomes to confuse admiration with instruction. Someone else’s success does not mean their personality, methods or priorities should automatically be copied. People can learn from mentors, colleagues and public figures without becoming replicas of them. Influence should ideally help someone understand themselves better rather than gradually replace their individuality.Think honestly about the choices you make and where they come from. A career may have been chosen because it genuinely interests you, or because it sounds impressive to other people. A creative idea may have changed because it became better, or because somebody else’s version received more attention. Before changing something about yourself, ask whether the change takes you closer to the person you want to become or simply closer to the person you think others will approve of. Being yourself “in the most vivid possible way” can begin with smaller decisions that still feel like your own when nobody else is watching.Streep’s observation continues to resonate because it reduces two enormous goals — happiness and success — to a question of identity. People spend years searching for the right career, relationship, lifestyle or formula for achievement, but the same answer cannot work for everyone because people do not share the same values or ambitions. Her words do not reject hard work, ambition or change; they suggest those things become more meaningful when they grow from a life that still feels recognisably your own. The message is simple: learn from others, keep growing and pursue what matters to you, but do not become so focused on somebody else’s version of success that you disappear from your own.
Article Summary: Quote of the day by meryl streep. “the formula of happiness and success is just, being actually yourself, in the most vivid possible way you can.” on the surface, it sounds like familiar advice about being yourself. But the deeper message is about resisting the pressure to build a life around somebody else’s expectations.

Article Title: Quote of the day by William Shakespeare: "All the world's a stage, and all the men and women merely..." - a timeless lesson on change, identity and life
Article Text:
William Shakespeare (Image: Wikipedia)

Quote of the day by William Shakespeare

"All the world's a stage, and all the men and women merely players. They have their exits and their entrances, and one man in his time plays many parts."

Written for a theatre whose own motto made the same claim

A simple way to actually use this idea

Other famous quotes by William Shakespeare

"To be, or not to be: that is the question."

"The fault, dear Brutus, is not in our stars, but in ourselves."

"We know what we are, but know not what we may be."

Two people can look at their own life story and understand its shape in completely different ways. One sees a single, continuous identity, the same person carrying the same fixed role from beginning to end, expected to remain recognisably consistent throughout. The other sees something closer to a sequence of distinct roles, each one genuinely different from the last, entered and exited on a schedule nobody fully controls. Shakespeare puts this second view into the mouth of Jaques, a famously melancholy character in As You Like It, who follows this opening line with what has become known as the "Seven Ages of Man" speech, tracing a single life from infancy through old age as a series of separate parts, the infant, the schoolboy, the lover, the soldier, the judge, the aging man, and finally a return to a kind of second childhood, each performed and then set aside as the next one begins.What gives this line extra resonance is where it was almost certainly first performed. As You Like It was written around 1599, likely staged at the Globe Theatre, the open-air playhouse built that same year for Shakespeare's own company, the Lord Chamberlain's Men. Tradition holds that the Globe carried a Latin motto over its entrance, "Totus mundus agit histrionem," roughly translating to "the whole world plays the actor," a phrase that made the theatre's own architecture a literal, physical echo of the line Jaques speaks on its stage.Audiences watching actors play multiple roles across an afternoon, in a building built around exactly that idea, would have felt the metaphor collapse the usual distance between the stage and the world outside it.It matters, too, that this speech comes from Jaques specifically, a character other figures in the play repeatedly describe as melancholic and given to overly cynical observations about life. The speech is not presented as simple, comforting wisdom. It sits inside a comedy that elsewhere shows real warmth, love, and reconciliation between its characters, which makes Jaques's bleak, theatrical view of life as a string of interchangeable roles feel like one perspective among several the play offers, rather than Shakespeare's own final word on the matter.The useful move here is loosening the grip of any single identity a person has been holding onto past its natural point: a role at work, a family position, a self-image formed years earlier, by recognising that a life is genuinely made up of distinct chapters rather than one unbroken performance. Treating an old role as permanent, once its actual season has passed, can make the ordinary process of change feel like a personal failure rather than simply the next scene arriving on schedule.A fair test, when a role or identity starts to feel like a poor fit for where you actually are now, is to ask whether you are still performing that particular part out of habit, or whether it's genuinely time for an exit and a new entrance. That question won't make any transition painless. It usually makes it feel less like a crisis and more like exactly what Jaques was describing all along.
Article Summary: William shakespeare's as you like it was written around 1599. It was likely staged at the globe theatre, the open-air playhouse built that same year. Tradition holds that the globe carried a latin motto over its entrance, "totus mundus agit histrionem" roughly translating to "the whole world plays the actor"

Article Title: Shattering records and cultivating future stars
Article Text:
Mayura Shanbaug

Ashish Kumar Srivastava - MD and CEO of PNB MetLife

Sameer Bansal - Chief Distribution Officer of PNB MetLife

Chirag Shetty - Asian Games Gold Medalist & JBC 2023 mentor

Satwiksairaj Rankireddy - Asian Games Gold Medalist & JBC 2023 mentor

Disclaimer: Content Produced by PNB Metlife

The 7th PNB MetLife Junior Badminton Championship shattered records with over 8,200 young talent nationwide, earning global recognition and fostering a culture of resilience and determination in aspiring badminton starsIn a spectacular display of badminton prowess and youthful enthusiasm, the 7th edition of the PNB MetLife Junior Badminton Championship (JBC) etched its name in the annals of sporting history. Celebrating a staggering participation of 8257 young champions from across India, the championship not only broke its own record set in 2022 but also clinched the title of the ‘Most kids participating in a Badminton Championship in multiple cities’ as recognised by the World Record Certification Agency (WRCA).The grand finale unfolded at the Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium in New Delhi, where the air was thick with competition, camaraderie, and the unmistakable passion for badminton. The event, graced by chief guests Chirag Shetty and Satwik Rankireddy, Asian Games Gold Medalists and JBC 2023 mentors, was a true celebration of the sport’s rising stars.The 10-city extravaganza, spanning the length and breadth of the country, showcased the unwavering commitment of PNB MetLife in nurturing young talents in the badminton arena. With participants exceeding 8200, it’s evident that the PNB MetLife JBC has become a beacon for aspiring shuttlers, highlighting the deep-seated passion for badminton among the diverse and talented youth of India.Beyond the glitz and glamour of the record-breaking numbers, the championship holds a special place in the hearts of those at the helm. Ashish Kumar Srivastava, MD and CEO of PNB MetLife, expressed pride in not just surpassing their own world record but also in contributing to India’s glory on the international badminton stage. The championship, he emphasized, is not merely a competition but a significant milestone in creating a pan-India badminton ecosystem.This edition of the JBC saw a strategic partnership with world champions Chirag Shetty and Satwiksairaj Rankireddy, who served as mentors for the young talents. Sameer Bansal, Chief Distribution Officer of PNB MetLife, acknowledged the pivotal role played by these champions in inspiring the next generation of badminton stars. The focus, according to Bansal, is on unleashing the latent potential of young shuttlers and preparing them for global excellence.The Delhi chapter of the championship witnessed some nail-biting action with over 1000 participants competing fiercely across various categories. From Ananya Talyan’s stellar performance in Girls Singles Under 9 to Divyansh Rawat’s triumph in Boys Singles Under 17, the young talents left no shuttle unturned in their quest for victory.The results from the Delhi leg not only showcased the raw talent but also highlighted the championship’s commitment to breaking barriers. The PNB MetLife Junior Badminton Championship is not just about records; it’s about fostering a culture of healthy living, determination, and resilience among the future champions of the sport.In the words of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy, the championship serves as an invaluable platform.---------------------------------------------------------------As we celebrate the successful culmination of the 7th edition of PNB MetLife Junior Badminton Championship , we take pride in surpassing our own world record for highest participation and for being recognized by World Record Certification Agency. Beyond the records, JBC represents a significant milestone in our mission to lay the groundwork for India’ s glory and success on the international badminton stage by creating a pan-India badminton ecosystem that nurtures champions at the grassroots levelThis year has been especially remarkable for PNB MetLife JBC as we joined hands with world champions Chirag Shetty and Satwiksairaj Rankireddy as JBC Mentors for the young talents associated with this tournament. They have played a pivotal role in inspiring young shuttlers to dream big and elevate their game and skills. We are eager for the next edition to unfold in our journey of unveiling the latent badminton potential across our nation and preparing them for global excellenceIt’s inspiring to witness the boundless talent and enthusiasm within our young athletes. My journey as JBC mentor has been incredibly fulfilling, as I got the opportunity to guide these budding champions and witness the journey of these young badminton stars. This championship is more than a competition; it is a platform that nurtures dreams, ignites aspirations, and, I believe, it is laying the foundation for future gold medalists in the makingTournaments like these serve as an invaluable platform for nurturing and harnessing the potential of our country’s young badminton stars. Witnessing the enthusiasm, passion, and skill displayed by these emerging shuttlers reinforces the belief that our country has an immense reservoir of talent. My association as a JBC mentor has been a source of immense pride, particularly given the role that the championship is playing in creating an incredible platform that is serving as a powerful catalyst, empowering young players and bolstering their confidence to become future champions
Article Summary: The 7th pnb metlife junior badminton championship shattered records with over 8,200 young talent nationwide. The grand finale unfolded at the indira gandhi indoor stadium in new delhi, where the air was thick with competition, camaraderie, and the unmistakable passion for badminton.

Article Title: Clash of Clans adds WWE characters and John Cena village hunt for September event: What it means for players
Article Text:
Cody Rhodes asks Clash of Clans players to find John Cena’s village

How to find John Cena's village

Six WWE characters

Cody Rhodes as the Barbarian King

Alexa Bliss as the Archer Queen

The Undertaker as the Grand Warden

Iyo Sky as the Royal Champion

Jey Uso as the Minion Prince

Kane as the Dragon Duke

WWE-themed features in Clash of Clans

Clash of Clans and WWE have launched their second collaboration, with players able to search for and raid John Cena’s in-game village throughout September. The event runs from September 1 to September 30 and also adds six WWE Superstars as Clash of Clans characters.The crossover centres on a fictional rivalry between WWE Superstars Cody Rhodes and John Cena, who are both described as long-time Clash of Clans players. Rhodes has enlisted other WWE Superstars and the game's players to help locate Cena's village.Players can encounter Cena's loot-filled base during their daily raids between September 1 and September 30. A successful raid can also earn players a Cody Rhodes statue for their in-game village.The search also features support from WWE personalities including The Undertaker and Iyo Sky, who are part of the event alongside Rhodes.The crossover adds six WWE Superstars reimagined as Clash of Clans Hero characters:Cody Rhodes returns as the Barbarian King following his appearance in the previous WWE collaboration.The event also introduces temporary troops and a WWE-themed village design based on WWE Money in the Bank. Players can additionally earn rewards from WWE chests, including Action Figure Equipment, Challenge Tickets and a Cody Rhodes skin.Players who already own the Cody Rhodes skin will receive alternative rewards, including a random Gold Pass skin, random Equipment or a Book of Everything, depending on which items they have already collected.
Article Summary: Cody rhodes asks clash of clans players to find john cena’s village. Players can encounter cena's loot-filled base during their daily raids. A successful raid can also earn players a cody rhodes statue. The event runs from september 1 to september 30.
